{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "partially_feasible_premise_rejected",
    "answerable": [
      "Estimate simulated groundwater recharge (bottom-layer drainage / deep percolation) at multiple representative points in the Naches River basin, WA.",
      "Quantify how recharge VARIES across elevation, climate, and soil texture within the basin.",
      "Test whether any single point yields ~500 mm/yr and whether a basin-wide uniform value is defensible."
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "We cannot 'confirm' that recharge is exactly 500 mm/yr EVERYWHERE. This premise is physically implausible: recharge is strongly modulated by precipitation gradients, snowpack, soil texture, and topography, so a spatially uniform exact value is not a testable/confirmable hypothesis. The simulations are designed instead to characterize the true spatial spread and to falsify the uniform-500 claim if warranted.",
      "Absolute recharge validation against observations is not possible without site-specific recharge/water-table or lysimeter data, which are not provided."
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 5,
  "n_justification": "The Naches basin spans a steep west-to-east orographic gradient from the Cascade crest (>1500 mm/yr precip, snow-dominated) down to the semi-arid Yakima confluence (~200 mm/yr, rain-dominated). Five columns sample this precipitation/elevation transect plus contrasting soil textures to expose spatial recharge variability and directly test the 'uniform 500 mm/yr' claim.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "cascade_crest_forest", "lat": 46.86, "lon": -121.40, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "upper_naches_montane", "lat": 46.98, "lon": -121.10, "soil_texture": "loam"},
    {"id": "mid_naches_valley", "lat": 46.83, "lon": -120.90, "soil_texture": "silt_loam"},
    {"id": "lower_naches_shrubsteppe", "lat": 46.73, "lon": -120.70, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "yakima_confluence_arid", "lat": 46.62, "lon": -120.55, "soil_texture": "silty_clay_loam"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1991",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2020",
    "STOP_N": "30",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "1991-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "QRECHARGE",
      "QDRAI",
      "QDRAI_PERCH",
      "QOVER",
      "QRUNOFF",
      "QINFL",
      "RAIN",
      "SNOW",
      "QFLX_EVAP_TOT",
      "QSNOMELT",
      "H2OSNO",
      "SOILLIQ",
      "SOILICE",
      "ZWT",
      "WA",
      "TWS"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": ["elm_singlecolumn", "datm_gswp3_or_daymet_forcing"],
  "assumptions": [
    "Recharge is diagnosed primarily from QRECHARGE (flux into the unconfined aquifer) with QDRAI as a cross-check; annual sums are averaged over the 30-yr climatology after a 10-yr spin-up discard.",
    "Column coordinates approximate a Cascade-to-Yakima transect through the Naches River basin, WA; each uses default ELM soil/PFT for its grid unless site data are supplied.",
    "30-year 1991-2020 forcing (GSWP3 or Daymet) captures interannual climate variability needed to bracket recharge, not a single-year snapshot.",
    "The experiment is framed to characterize spatial variability and to TEST (potentially falsify) the uniform-500-mm/yr claim rather than presume it; a run of subsurface flow in PFLOTRAN could be added if lateral/deep transport confirmation is required."
  ]
}

answerable: Estimate simulated groundwater recharge (bottom-layer drainage / deep percolation) at multiple representative points in the Naches River basin, WA.
Quantify how recharge VARIES across elevation, climate, and soil texture within the basin.
Test whether any single point yields ~500 mm/yr and whether a basin-wide uniform value is defensible.
not_answerable: We cannot 'confirm' that recharge is exactly 500 mm/yr EVERYWHERE. This premise is physically implausible: recharge is strongly modulated by precipitation gradients, snowpack, soil texture, and topography, so a spatially uniform exact value is not a testable/confirmable hypothesis. The simulations are designed instead to characterize the true spatial spread and to falsify the uniform-500 claim if warranted.
Absolute recharge validation against observations is not possible without site-specific recharge/water-table or lysimeter data, which are not provided.

parsed.n_justification: The Naches basin spans a steep west-to-east orographic gradient from the Cascade crest (>1500 mm/yr precip, snow-dominated) down to the semi-arid Yakima confluence (~200 mm/yr, rain-dominated). Five columns sample this precipitation/elevation transect plus contrasting soil textures to expose spatial recharge variability and directly test the 'uniform 500 mm/yr' claim.
assumptions: Recharge is diagnosed primarily from QRECHARGE (flux into the unconfined aquifer) with QDRAI as a cross-check; annual sums are averaged over the 30-yr climatology after a 10-yr spin-up discard.
Column coordinates approximate a Cascade-to-Yakima transect through the Naches River basin, WA; each uses default ELM soil/PFT for its grid unless site data are supplied.
30-year 1991-2020 forcing (GSWP3 or Daymet) captures interannual climate variability needed to bracket recharge, not a single-year snapshot.

The experiment is framed to characterize spatial variability and to TEST (potentially falsify) the uniform-500-mm/yr claim rather than presume it; a run of subsurface flow in PFLOTRAN could be added if lateral/deep transport confirmation is required.
